quest.title: The Price of Every Price
quest.description: A message arrives from the Palais Mermonia. Seems like it's time to make a move.
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x20, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

talks.objective: Wait until the morning of the day after tomorrow (08:00 – 10:00)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, everyone! We're not late, are we?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: No, you're just in time. Well rested, I trust?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Staying busy keeps you sharp.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: A great way to stay energetic, certainly.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you all started preparing?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: We received word from Mr. Argenteau yesterday, confirming the time and location of the transaction.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: It'll take place this afternoon. And it turns out it'll be somewhere we all know pretty well, too — the Film Fantasyland restaurant.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh really? Huh, he sure does like that place...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: #Seems like you share our concerns, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Indeed. Capturing someone in a crowded event venue will be much more challenging than in an open area.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The criminal might try to blend in with the crowd, or even escape by taking hostages.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: In light of this, we've had to make additional preparations. As soon as we received the news yesterday, we began coordinating with the Marechaussee Phantom and the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm. We'll be deploying lots of undercover agents on-site. If things go south, the safety of the civilians will be our top priority.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Of course, fingers crossed, everything will go without a hitch.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I noticed a bunch of familiar faces from the previous case, like Captain Chevreuse of the Special Patrol. So I'm feeling optimistic.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: We'll trust your instincts, then.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, and by the way, we've also been in communication with Miss Lepine-Pauline and Miss Navia.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The Spina di Rosula will provide support within a controlled scope, so there's no need to worry.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: The only potential issue... is with Miss Escoffier.

choices.text: She doesn't want to serve criminals?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Haha, it would be easy if it were that simple.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Ahem...

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Alright, no more jokes. Miss Escoffier has made it clear that she doesn't want her restaurant to suffer any losses as a result of this operation.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: But, uh... Haha, well, I have a feeling things might not go quite as smoothly as she hopes.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is there anything I can do?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: To be honest, we shouldn't have dragged you into this in the first place, and it's caused you quite enough trouble already. The Fontainian authorities should be able to handle the rest from here.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: But still, I'm guessing you'd like to see how it all turns out.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Definitely.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Well then, feel free to head down to the scene, but just stay alert and play it by ear. You won't necessarily have to do anything — unless things go pear-shaped, of course.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: I'll do my best to ensure that things don't escalate to that point.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're getting involved too, Kinich?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Of course.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: There are still a lot of unanswered questions, but our intel so far indicates that the culprit's from Natlan.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Plus, I'm already a witness in this case. Might as well see this thing through to the end.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, that's the Kinich we know and love!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The group go on to discuss the specifics of the operation and things to watch out for.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: For once, the conversation goes surprisingly smoothly... Perhaps because Ajaw and Cacucu aren't present.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: It's just as well, really. Things could've gotten awkward if Ajaw showed up and started cursing out Neuvillette...

choices.text: She wants to introduce them to her chopping board?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: You know what, that might not be such a bad idea...

talks.objective: Go to the area near the Palais Mermonia

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This beach seems to be getting livelier by the day!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Thanks in part, surely, to the undercover agents.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, um...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahem! Paimon's getting kinda hungry... Let's go check out the restaurant menu, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The guy with the case... that's got to be him.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Alright, it's business time.)

dialogues.speaker: Angoulvant
dialogues.text: Unbelievable! You can't just drag someone around like that! Such blatant disregard for human life... I'm gonna sue the living daylights outta you!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Will you now?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I think I did you a favor by pulling you away from your "audience." Saved you some face, at the very least.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: As for whether you were facing up or down along the way... Well, that was your decision, wasn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Angoulvant
dialogues.text: Why you...!

dialogues.speaker: Angoulvant
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, I admit it, I was in the wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Angoulvant
dialogues.text: *sigh* Of course I know the difference between right and wrong. But I had no choice... I desperately needed the money.

dialogues.speaker: Angoulvant
dialogues.text: I was an expert on ancient relics... Not only did I have a successful career, but a happy family too.

dialogues.speaker: Angoulvant
dialogues.text: But my son... I never imagined he'd turn out this way. Fell in with the wrong crowd and ended up shoulder-deep in gambling... We had some savings, but he drained them away like a waterfall!

dialogues.speaker: Angoulvant
dialogues.text: Once he fell into debt, he had creditors regularly coming over to threaten and intimidate him... I'm his father. How could I just stand by and watch him suffer like that?

dialogues.speaker: Angoulvant
dialogues.text: *sigh* My son is about the same age as you are! If only he could have turned out more like you... That's the only reason I needed the money, please believe me!

dialogues.speaker: Angoulvant
dialogues.text: You...

dialogues.speaker: Angoulvant
dialogues.text: Please, kid, I'm begging you, help me!

dialogues.speaker: Angoulvant
dialogues.text: I see you're from Natlan too... That makes us brothers! Please, have mercy!

dialogues.speaker: Angoulvant
dialogues.text: I still have a chance to help my son straighten himself out — but only if I get back. If I go to prison now, he'll be doomed, I tell you, doomed!

dialogues.speaker: Angoulvant
dialogues.text: And isn't standing together and fighting for a better future what families do?

dialogues.speaker: Angoulvant
dialogues.text: Our fate is in your hands, young man. Please, have a heart!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Haha, something wrong, Kinich? Gone soft, have we?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Hmph.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I don't believe a word you say.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Wriothesley had you just about figured out — you're a gambler, pure and simple.

dialogues.speaker: Angoulvant
dialogues.text: A gambler? Me? Nonsense! I told you, it's... it's my son—

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: First of all, are you really from Natlan?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: You've been keeping tabs on the gun's whereabouts this whole time — you should have recognized at least one familiar face by now.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: On top of that, the way you threatened to sue me? Spoken like a true Fontainian, if you ask me.

dialogues.speaker: Angoulvant
dialogues.text: Huh? What kind of logic is that...

dialogues.speaker: Angoulvant
dialogues.text: I—I can explain! I... I actually grew up in, in—

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Tsk. I don't wanna hear another word.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Ajaw, here's your chance. Shut someone else up for once.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Hahahahaha, the moment I've been waiting for!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Eat this, scumbag!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Being a compulsive liar is one of the hallmarks of a diehard gambler.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I bet you're just a Fontainian pretending to be from Natlan. Even if you have any friends or family to speak of, I'm guessing they've long since cut all ties with you — and you have your depraved ways to thank for that.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Of course, I might be wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: But does that matter?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I'm just here to arrest you. If you're looking for an advocate or a shoulder to cry on, you're out of luck.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Besides, prying the truth out of you is exactly what your beloved courts are for. Isn't that right?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: It's been a while, Mr. Kinich. The Special Patrol will take this criminal off your hands now.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Many thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Please. I should be the one thanking you for all the help you've given us.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: And me? Hmm, hmm? What about me? Hmph, so rude! You should be bowing down in gratitude to the Almighty Dragonlord!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: As you wish. My thanks to you, and also to Mr. Cacucu, for your show-stopping performances.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Hey, what do you mean!? Hold it right there!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you okay, Kinich?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'm fine. I wasn't the one who just got dragged all the way here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You seemed a little upset just now.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Pfft... Little Kinich, thinking back to when you were just an itty bitty boy Kinich, aren't ya?

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Aw, don't start crying like a little baby! I am the Almighty Dragonlord! No servant of mine will be seen acting so weak and pathetic in public!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: What are you on about...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Bad Ajaw, bad.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Still, I suppose there's no point hiding it from you. To put it plainly, I can't stand gamblers.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: They're the most irresponsible people in the entire world... No respect for the principle that you have to give in order to get.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: They'll tell a thousand lies for a single coin, deluding themselves into thinking they can use it to gamble their way to a vast fortune.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: But we all know that even when it looks like you're getting something for free, there's always an unseen cost.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: In the past, I also ended up paying a price for my father's gambling losses. I don't want anyone else to end up in a similar situation if I can help it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Kinich...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Don't feel sorry for me. I certainly don't feel sorry for myself.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: They say that people are shaped by their past. And since I've made it this far... I must have done a lot of things right.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: We should never punish ourselves for the mistakes of others.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Instead, I choose to remember the moments that helped me grow.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Like when I first learned to use a grappling hook...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Or the very first time I yearned for knowledge.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I get it.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Yeah, I believe you.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Let's get going. If we don't head back soon, we'll cause more unnecessary worry.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yay, {NICKNAME}, Kinich, you're back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We just saw Chevreuse taking the criminal away. She looked pretty pleased with herself!

choices.text: Well, it did go smoother than expected.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, so after so much running in circles, turns out he had no fight in him, huh? Guess running away was the only trick up his sleeve!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, also, Wriothesley said to let you know that he's already left. He went to report back to the Palais Mermonia.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Apparently, the Marechaussee Phantom's preparing to carry out an in-depth investigation into illegal gambling activities. Sounds like they'll have their hands full...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, that's for the Palais to worry about. Not really our concern.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Judging by how fast the Duke took off, I'd say he was avoiding my Kamera!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: *sigh* But I guess I'm used to that by now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, it's not like you to give up so easily, Charlotte!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Hehe, it's fine — I got plenty of other great shots back there. More than enough for a front-page spread!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: And on that note, this busy reporter needs to scoot. Those photos won't develop themselves!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Make sure you pick the best shots of Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, already gone... Hope she heard that...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You can trust her judgment, Paimon. She's a professional photographer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you're right!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But what took you all so long to get here? Did something happen?

choices.text: Ajaw bonked his head and started crying.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: What!?

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Rumors and slander!

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: When have I, the Almighty Dragonlord, K'uhul Ajaw, ever sunk to such sniveling?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Often, actually.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Anyway... What's next?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Hmm... To be honest, I haven't decided yet.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: At the moment, I've got nothing urgent to get back for. And in any case, the court might need me to testify again.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Plus, that gun's still a key piece of evidence. I'll probably have to wait until the case is closed before I can return it to Natlan.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: So I guess I'll be sticking around to enjoy the beach a little longer.

choices.text: Kinich hit his head and started crying.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: If you say so.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Hahaha! Poor little Kinich! No one was there to pat him on the head, so he went off to cry all on his own...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: For real, now? Seems more likely that Ajaw was the one crying...

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Hey, you little—!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Neuvillette sent someone to contact us this morning!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That must mean there's been some progress. No time to waste, let's head out!
